transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I'm here because I feel like I'm constantly on the go, almost like I'm driven by a motor. I just can't seem to slow down or relax, and it's really starting to wear me out.
Have you felt this way for as long as you can remember, dating back to your childhood, or does this feeling come and go in distinct periods or episodes?

Yes, I've definitely had this feeling since I was a kid, well before I turned twelve. It doesn't really come and go in episodes, though; it has been completely constant for the last year and two months.
Along with feeling constantly on the go, do you also struggle with things like staying focused, being easily distracted, or organizing your tasks?
No, I don't really struggle with staying focused, being distracted, or keeping things organized. My main issue is definitely just feeling constantly on the go and active all the time.
Do you also experience excessive, hard-to-control worry or anxiety about everyday things, or is this feeling purely a physical need to keep moving?
No, I don't have any excessive worry or anxiety about everyday things. It's purely a physical need to keep moving, like I'm constantly on the go and driven by a motor.
How have these difficulties with being constantly on the go affected your daily life, such as at work, at home, or in your relationships?

I haven't really thought about it in detail, so I'm not quite sure how to describe its specific impact on my work, home, or relationships. All I know is that I simply feel constantly on the go, as if I am being driven by a motor all day long.
Besides feeling constantly on the go, do you also find yourself fidgeting a lot, talking excessively, or having difficulty waiting your turn?
I wouldn't say I fidget a lot, but I definitely talk excessively and often find myself interrupting others or butting into their conversations. It's just really hard for me to wait my turn to speak.
Have family members, friends, or coworkers ever complained about or commented on your constant activity or your tendency to interrupt?

Yes, absolutely, people comment on it all the time. My family and coworkers often tell me that I'm always 'on the go' as if driven by a motor, and I frequently get complaints about interrupting others or butting into their conversations.
Do you notice these behaviors, like your constant activity and tendency to interrupt, happening in multiple areas of your life, such as both at home and at work?
I'm not entirely sure, as I haven't really thought much about whether it happens in specific multiple settings. I just know that it's a constant feeling for me overall.

These symptoms are persistent across settings and cause interpersonal difficulties, while symptoms of inattention are notably absent, supporting the diagnosis of ADHD, Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation.
